subject: Acme Health – DPA addendum: residency, subprocessors, and bounded failover
messages:
From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acme-health.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T16:12:00Z
Subject: DPA addendum + residency questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week. Before we move to an internal procurement review, our legal and privacy team have a few outstanding items we need clarified in writing so we can include them in the DPA addendum:

1) Data residency commitment: Can Redwood guarantee that customer production requests for EU-tagged data will not leave the EU for inference or key material usage, except under a documented, time-limited failover? If failover is possible, what are the exact conditions and maximum duration?

2) Subprocessors: please send the current roster (including cloud infra and any managed services that may process request logs). We need supplier names, country, and role.

3) KMS / key locality: Do you support customer-managed keys where the key residency is in the EU? If not, can you provide an attestation of where KMS material is held and who has access?

4) Auditability: We will likely require 30-day prior notice for any change affecting residency guarantees and a ledger of any cross-region events that includes affected request IDs and justification.

Attached is our standard questionnaire (Acme_Questionnaire_v2.pdf) with some fields prefilled. Can you confirm what you can sign and provide a proposed DPA clause for bounded failover (language we can present to our counsel)?

Appreciate a prompt reply — we are aiming to finalize procurement terms by mid-November.

Best,
Sara
Sara Nguyen
Data Privacy Lead, Acme Health

--
Attachment: Acme_Questionnaire_v2.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-10-28T17:04:00Z
Subject: FW: DPA addendum + residency questions (Acme Health)

Team — forwarding Acme's questionnaire. They want explicit residency guarantees and a bounded failover clause. Quick thoughts and owners:

- Marissa (Legal/Product): can we draft a short addendum that: (a) confirms region-pinning for production traffic by default, (b) includes a bounded failover exception with notification + logging, and (c) offers a 30-day change notice for subprocessors impacting residency? They are explicit about signed language.

- Jonas (Infra): what level of assurance can we give on IP layer and KMS material? Can we support customer-managed keys with EU-only HSMs for this account? If not, what mitigations (attestation + access controls) do we have? Also need the subprocessor roster export.

- Karthik (SRE/Products ops): how long would a failover window need to be in practice for a cross-region mitigation (e.g., region-wide outage)? Proposal options below — please comment with feasibility and expected RTO/RPO impacts:
  Option A — Strict pin: no cross-border processing for customer production traffic; failover requires manual approval and contractual SLA exception.
  Option B — Bounded failover: automatic failover allowed for up to N hours (we should propose a number) with full audit logs and customer notification within T minutes.
  Option C — Hybrid: inference pinned; non-sensitive telemetry/analytics may be processed in US with opt-out.

Deliverable ask from me: I will prepare a proposed addendum draft and a short routing-playbook we can include with the DPA. Jonas — please attach the current subprocessor_roster_oct2026.csv and a short note on where KMS material resides today. Marissa — can you flag any existing clauses we cannot change?

Let's get a single-slide summary for Acme (one-pager) and a proposed legal paragraph they can show counsel. Can we target EOD Friday (2026-10-30) for the internal draft? If not, earliest next business day.

Thanks,
Naomi
Director, Enterprise Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acme-health.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T14:22:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA addendum + residency questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the quick ring-up and for looping in your legal/infra folks. A few clarifications from our side that will help the addendum wording:

- Bounded failover is acceptable to Acme if the following conditions are met: (1) failover is limited to 72 hours maximum per incident, (2) every failover event is logged with request IDs and a root-cause note, and (3) we receive written notification within 24 hours of the event start.
- We require the subprocessor roster with country and role (not just vendor name).
- On KMS: if you cannot support customer-managed keys resident in the EU, we need an attestation describing where key material is held, which personnel or teams have access, and the contractual controls in place.

If you can provide the addendum language and the roster + attestation this week, we will expedite internal sign-off.

Regards,
Sara

--
Reply-to: dp-team@acme-health.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Nguyen <sara.nguyen@acme-health.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T22:04:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA addendum + residency questions

Sara — thanks for the clarity. Below is the plan and proposed DPA paragraph we believe addresses Acme's requirements. Attaching the subprocessor roster and routing playbook draft for your review.

Planned deliverables and timelines:
- Subprocessor roster (with country + role): attached (subprocessor_roster_oct2026.csv). Delivered now.
- KMS attestation: Jonas to provide short attestation by 2026-11-02. Current state: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via partner HSMs; for EU regions keys are stored in EU-managed HSMs in our EU cloud region. Full attestation to include access controls and personnel lists (redacted) will be provided.
- Addendum draft: proposed DPA paragraph below; Marissa will circulate a formal addendum for signature by 2026-11-03.
- Technical test: We will enable a staging demo of region pin enforcement and a simulated failover within a customer-scoped sandbox on 2026-11-05 (invite to follow).

Proposed DPA paragraph (for counsel):
"Redwood Inference will, for Account requests designated as EU-resident data, route and process Production inference requests only within geographic infrastructure located in the European Union, except where an explicit, documented bounded failover occurs as described below. In the event of an infrastructure outage or emergent operational condition that prevents continued processing within the EU region, Redwood may failover processing to non-EU infrastructure for a period not to exceed seventy-two (72) consecutive hours per incident. Redwood will: (a) provide written notification to Customer within twenty-four (24) hours of initiating such failover; (b) log and provide, upon request, the set of affected request IDs and a brief root-cause description; and (c) take commercially reasonable steps to minimize cross-border processing and to return processing to EU infrastructure as soon as reasonably practicable."

If that text looks acceptable I will have Marissa prep the formal addendum and Jonas will complete the KMS attestation. We will also include the routing_playbook_draft.pdf as an appendix to the addendum.

Next steps for Acme: confirm acceptance of the 72-hour bounded failover and the 24-hour notification window. If you prefer a shorter window we can discuss, but we want to ensure operationally safe SLAs.

Thanks — will follow up with the legal draft shortly.

Best,
Naomi
Director, Enterprise Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
